A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Causal Delta Embedding work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original CDE experiments on ProcTHOR and Epic-Kitchens, including accuracy results, component ablations, hyperparameter studies, and representation analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and reports additional backbone configurations, revised accuracy results, and ablation findings.

M1.justification: The specified patch-wise training objective changes: v1 averages the selected patch deltas before applying the loss, whereas v2 Section 5.2.1 applies the loss to each selected delta and averages the losses. This is a localized procedural revision; the global model, delta subtraction, three loss components, and top-K selection principle remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate single-object and multi-object ProcTHOR and real-world Epic-Kitchens using the same compositional and systematic shift scenarios. The additional backbone configurations do not introduce new evaluated datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 removes the k-NN-versus-MLP comparison from v1 Figure 10. Its loss-ablation table newly includes the Liu et al. baseline with 0.47 OOD accuracy, although that comparator already appears in the main benchmark comparison. The main benchmark comparator sets otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds CLIP and MAE ViT-B/16 evaluation configurations alongside the retained DINO backbone, and removes the auxiliary k=5 nearest-neighbor testing procedure. The stated benchmark splits, accuracy metrics, preprocessing, and optimization budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Backbone sensitivity evidence expands from the ResNet/DINO comparison to DINO, CLIP, and MAE configurations across the benchmark settings, while component-ablation findings are revised. V1's neighborhood-quality analysis using k-NN is removed entirely. The loss-weight and top-K sweeps, transformation-vector analysis, heatmaps, and UMAP analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results use means and standard deviations over three independent runs with different random seeds. V2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, or significance tests; changed standard-deviation values are result changes.

E6.justification: Reported DINO single-object systematic OOD accuracy changes from 0.73 to 0.75. The CE-only ablation changes from 0.59 to 0.67, reducing the full-model advantage from 14 to 8 percentage points. V2 adds CLIP/MAE result rows across settings, revises some patch-wise IID and uncertainty entries, and removes the k-NN results. The added backbone scores represent additional configurations, not matched-setting gains.

T1.justification: V2 explicitly adopts additive structural noise and replaces Equation 3's small Gaussian perturbation with independent zero-mean noise. Appendix E adds a logistic-regression derivation showing that zero weights on independent noise features minimize expected cross-entropy. V1 left deeper analysis of actionable counterfactuals to future work; this is substantive new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that sparse, context-invariant delta representations improve OOD action prediction on Causal Triplet and reveal opposing-action geometry. Foregrounding actionable counterfactuals and describing CDE as an approach rather than a theoretical framework do not materially alter these main scientific claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds a tentative explanation linking weak ResNet performance to inadequate disentanglement and makes noisy-case applicability conditional on independent zero-mean noise. Appendix B.1 newly qualifies the opposing-action interpretation using add/remove similarity 0.19, already visible in v1's heatmap. The limitations concerning low real-world accuracy and context-dependent transformations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds backbone architectures, pretraining information, parameter counts, and timm usage in Appendix D.5, plus implementation descriptions for the already-evaluated Slot baselines in Appendix F. It newly discloses smaller subsets for appendix ablations and states that code accompanies supplementary material. These disclosures do not establish changed sampling or independently verify code availability.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially broaden coverage of score-based identifiability, unknown multi-node interventions, invariance-based CRL, causal contrastive learning, and mechanism sparsity. Added discussions include Varici/Varıcı, Yao, Buchholz, and Lachapelle works, developing the relationship between intervention embeddings and these research directions beyond v1's shorter positioning.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the introduction and related work, converts much of the enumerated architecture and loss exposition into prose, and introduces hierarchical section numbering and organized Appendices A–F. It also adds a dedicated actionable-counterfactual subsection, reproducibility statement, and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. V1 Tables 2 and 3 become a combined dataset-grouped table, backbone rows and a specification table are added, and the heatmaps move from the main text to the appendix. Figures are resized and redistributed, while the k-NN comparison plot is removed.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the work easier to assess through broader backbone comparisons, the conditional noise derivation, more implementation details, and a qualification of opposing-action geometry. Table 1's systematic gap also becomes consistent with its reported accuracies. These gains are tempered by removal of the k-NN validation and unresolved alignment between Section 5.2.1's per-patch losses and Figure 3's aggregated-delta depiction. The noise proof is limited to logistic regression, so it does not establish a general guarantee for the trained nonlinear model.
